item.title: ’Eavy Metal takes on more colours with Warhammer Tone Pro paints
item.description: See more miniatures painted with the new paint range and learn their recipes.
item.content:encoded:
The Warhammer Tone Pro range of paints will be available to pre-order tomorrow. We’re rounding off our week looking at the different colours with a look at white and earthy shades of brown.

White Scars Intercessor

This Intercessor from the sons of the Khan has been basecoated with Blackstone Void 5. The shading and armour chipping has been done with Dataslate Grey 3 & 4 to give a warmer finish compared to the colder Blackstone Void paints. The red on the chest has been painted with Bloodtoof Red 3.

Knights Excelsior Liberator

This Liberator has also been painted with Blackstone Void 5, but the chipping and shading has been achieved using Gnarlwood 3 & 4.

Chaos Sorcerer Lord

Finally, we have a little bonus, showing off some other colours. The armour of the Chaos Sorcerer Lord has been painted with Blackstone Void 1 and then highlighted with Craventhrone Cloak 1, 2, 3, 4, & 5. The cloak is Gnarlwood 5, shaded with Gnarlwood 3, and highlighted with Necrolith Bone 3, 4, & 5. The magical green parts of the sword and staff were painted with Green Morkshroom 3, 4, & 5. The fur is basecoated with Necrolith Bone 2, which was shaded with Gnarlwood 3 & 4, and highlighted with Necrolith Bone 4 & 5. The gold was shaded with Carthalos Skin 3 (used with the Shading Medium), and the red binding on the staff was drybrushed with Carmine Blades 3 & 4, using the new Warhammer Pro Tone Dry Brush XS.

Now you’ve seen what the ’Eavy Metal team have done with the new paints, what will you try? The 150 new Warhammer Tone Pro paints and two new mediums will all be available to pre-order from tomorrow.

item.title: Peaks and Deeps – Take a Tour of a Khazalite Hold
item.description: Explore the subterranean dwellings of Warhammer Age of Sigmar’s newest faction.
item.content:encoded:
Back at the Big Autumn Preview, we unveiled a brand-new faction for Warhammer Age of Sigmar – the Khazalite Holds. But what is a ‘hold’, and what secrets do they hold? Let’s find out! 

Stocky and stout-hearted duardin, the Khazalites consider themselves the truest and most honourable of this race of warriors and master crafters. The mountains are their home, great holds known as karaks, hewn into the rock. While these subterranean settlements were meant to withstand the passage of time, many lie in ruins after centuries of strife and infiltration by malign forces.

Inside a Karak

Although every Khazalite hold is unique, many share similar characteristics, regardless of the realm they are in – particularly the upper halls above ground and subterranean lower halls, which are divided into areas known as ‘deeps’.

The Upper Halls

Above the surface, but still well within the mountain, the upper levels host the living quarters of those charged with guarding the karak, and are the first – and often only – areas outsiders will see.

The Outer Gate

Hewn into the side of the mountain and flanked by statues of the ancestors, the Outer Gate is the first marker of the karak. Its mighty and striking facade hints at the scale of what is behind – and beneath – it and, as with everything of duardin construction, is built with incredible skill and of the finest materials by master craftsmen.

The Oathkeeper Battery

Protecting the Outer Gate are concealed batteries of cannons and great defences manned by Clangunners, designed to deter would-be attackers from attempting to force entry through the runic archways which mark the entry to the karak proper. Additional sentinel points are often found cut into the highest peaks of the mountain, from which any approaching foes can be spotted.

Beyond the threshold, the upper halls are usually made up of massive thronghalls – barracks for the garrison of the upper levels of the karak. Within these great spaces are brewhalls, feasting chambers, and a wanderer’s hearth by which duardin and their allies who seek respite or shelter can be warmly welcomed.

The Deeps

The lower halls, or ‘deeps’, contain the main armouries, as well as the hearths and the royal throne room. They are a hive of industry as well as remembrance. 

The Resonance Chamber

Everything in the realms, down to the matter that makes up the land, has a vibrational frequency, which the Khazalites have managed to harness. Indeed, the Khazalites believe they can ‘hear’ stone and heed the wisdom from within it. This affinity with sound led the Khazalites to build great resonance chambers, filled with gongs and horns, the sounds of which echo from the ancestor statues.

The Hall of Remembrance

Most important of all to the Khazalites is remembrance. The ancient pantheon of Ancestor Gods are revered in great ceremony – their names and deeds uttered in the hope that they will grant strength, courage, or wisdom to the current and future generations. These acts of remembrance are carried out in great halls and chambers, where the stone echoes with the sounds of these solemn rites – for to be forgotten is the worst fate of all to these duardin. 

The Forge

The pounding heart of the karak is the great forge, where duardin toil endlessly to master their craft, while vast underground farms allow each hold to be self-sufficient, and gem mines satisfy the Khazalite need to delve and explore.

The Khazalite Holds Army Set, which includes a full Spearhead and the battletome, will be available to pre-order soon, but in the meantime, you can brush up on your duardin lore in Grombrindal: Ancestor’s Burden by Chris Thursten and Gotrek and Maleneth: The Omnibus, featuring tales by Darius Hinks and Robbie MacNiven.*


* Both titles are also available as eBooks via the Black Library app.

item.title: Liveries of the Legio Custodes during the Horus Heresy
item.description: Discover the lore behind the different colours of the Custodian Guard.
item.content:encoded:
The Legio Custodes are well known for their shining golden armour, but they’ve been shown wearing other colour schemes throughout the Age of Darkness. 

Today, we’re looking at some of the variants used during the Horus Heresy to inspire you to try something new.

The livery most associated with the demi-godlike warriors of the Legio Custodes has, since the Legio’s inception in the depths of Terran pre-history, been shining gold armour with deep red cloaks, loincloths and helmet plumes – a combination derived from the arms and devices of their master himself, the Emperor of Mankind. 

While this livery remains the standard, variants are known to exist, some of which are linked to one of the three ‘Templii Magisterium Tertia’. Each of the Templi is a loose sub-order of guardians aligned to a particular aspect of the overarching mission of the Legio Custodes, within which a Custodian might serve, sometimes for a single assignment, or in rare instances for an entire lifetime. Each of the Templii has associated with it a variation of the standard Custodes livery, and those Custodians assigned to special service with one of them are wont, on occasion, to don these unique colours in order to signal their dedication to that Templi’s specific mission. 

Suggested paints 

Gold armour 

● Base - Retributor Armour 

● Soft shade - Darkoath Flesh 

● Deep shade - Cygor Brown 

● Edge Highlight - Liberator Gold 

● Extreme edges - Stormhost Silver 

Light gold armour 

● Base - Liberator Gold 

● Soft shade - Wyldwood 

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Red cloth and plumes 

● Basecoat - Mephiston Red 

● Soft shade - Barak-Nar Burgundy 

● Deepshade - Barak-Nar Burgundy + Abaddon Black (selectively, mainly where separate bits of cloth meet) 

● Chunky Highlight - Evil Sunz Scarlet 

● Highlight - Wild Rider Red 

● Highlight - Wild Rider Red + Ungor Flesh 

● Highlight - Add more Ungor Flesh 

● Dots - Ungor Flesh 

● Smooth - Evil Sunz Scarlet 

Pteruges/red leather and gloves

● Base - Khorne Red + Doombull Brown 

● Shade - base + Abaddon Black 

● Chunky Highlight - Khorne Red 

● Highlight - Khorne Red 3:1 Fire Dragon Bright 

● Highlight - Khorne Red 2:1 Fire Dragon Bright 

● Highlight - Khorne Red 1:3 Fire Dragon Bright 

● Dots - Fire Dragon Bright 

(Above) A Custodian resplendent in the gold armour and red cloak and helmet plume most often worn by the majority of the Legio Custodes regardless of assignment. Being derived from the scheme worn by the Emperor himself throughout the Wars of Unity and much of the Great Crusade, this is what most of the Imperium would associate with the order.

(Above) A Caladius Annihilator grav-tank bearing the ubiquitous gold and red livery of the Legio Custodes. Note the inclusion of the battle-honour ‘Nordyc’ on the grav-tank’s flank, a memorial to but one of the numerous campaigns of the Wars of Unity in which it would have served. 

The Templii Magisterium Tertia 

The Legio Custodes is understood to have been divided into three distinct parts, each constituted to pursue a particular element of the Emperor’s Great Work, though it was not until the fateful years of the Scouring that the full, overarching extent of this structure could be speculated upon. Revealed only to a select few beyond the Imperial Household during the wars of the Horus Heresy, and all but unknown during the Great Crusade (at least in purpose and form, if not name), the trifold Templii Magisterium Tertia’s very existence suggests a far broader mandate for the Legio Custodes than was widely understood. 

The Templi Lictoris 

Perhaps the oldest of the three Templii, the Templi Lictoris embodied, in essence, the Custodians’ role as understood by the Imperium at large – as protectors of the Emperor’s person and his companions in war. 

During the Legio Custodes’ two centuries as the speartip of the Great Crusade, it was the warriors of the Templi Lictoris who stood at the Emperor’s side as he bestrode battlefields across the galaxy and brought innumerable worlds into Compliance, and in the aftermath of Magnus’ great folly, it was they who battled desperately to prevent the terrors of the Empyrean from breaching the Imperial Dungeon. One facet of the Templii Magisterium Tertia’s concealment from the wider Imperium for such a long period likely stems from the assumption (actively promoted by the Imperial Household) that the archetype inhabited by the Templi Lictoris was representative of the Legio Custodes entire, though this could not be further from the truth. 

While Custodians undertaking duties under the specific aegis of the Templi Lictoris might wear the standard gold and red of the Legio, those with particular associations with the Lictoris and its goals might adopt the scheme shown below. This features ivory white cloaks, plumes, and panel in-fills, along with black armour with a distinct iridescent finish.

Suggested paints 

Armour 

● Base - Iron Warriors 

● Soft Shade - Black Templar 

● Deep Shade - Abaddon Black 

● Highlight - Ironbreaker 

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Gold trim 

● Base - Liberator Gold 

● Soft shade - Wyldwood 

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Ivory cloaks & plumes 

● Base - Rakarth Flesh 2:1 Karak Stone 

● Soft shade - Karak Stone 

● Deep shade - Karak Stone 1:1 Dryad Bark 

● Chunky Highlight - Rakarth Flesh 

● Highlight - Rakarth Flesh 1:1 Pallid Wych Flesh 

● Highlight - Pallid Wych Flesh 

● Highlight/ Dot - White Scar 

Pteruges/ black leather and gloves 

● Base - Eshin Grey 

● Soft shade - Abaddon Black 

● Chunky Highlight - Skavenblight Dinge

● Highlight - Stormvermin Fur

● Highlight - Stormvermin Fur 1:1 Karak Stone 

● Highlight/Dot - Karak Stone

(Above) A Custodian resplendent in iridescent black and ivory white of the Templi Lictoris. 

The Templi Prudentia 

The first of the Templi Lictoris’ veiled counterparts was the Templi Prudentia, its duty being the security of the Emperor’s manifold and inscrutable plans, defending both the physical integrity of shadowed facilities across the Imperium as well as the secrecy of their contents. Their vigil safeguarded vaults laden with the weapons of Old Night, laboratories tasked with goals beyond comprehension, and prisons which entombed the Imperium’s most monstrous foes, and when the Emperor demanded some forbidden technology cloistered beyond the Imperium’s frontiers brought to Him, it was the warriors of the Templi Prudentia which saw it recovered. In the years of the Horus Heresy, both distant garrisons of the Templi Prudentia and fleets dispatched from Sol endeavoured to withhold such artefacts from the Traitors’ grasp, and at the fateful Siege of Terra, the Templi Prudentia is believed to have employed several nightmarish weapons once sequestered within their care against the Warmaster’s armies. 

Custodians operating under special service to the Templi Prudentia might on occasion adopt the scheme shown below, which employs fabric of purple and sometimes ivory white, purple in-fills, and polished black armour.

Suggested paints

Black armour 

● Basecoat - Abaddon Black 

● Chunky Highlight - Eshin Grey 1:1 Corvus Black 

● Highlight - Eshin Grey 

● Highlight - Dawnstone 

● Highlight - Administratum Grey 

● Spots - Administratum Grey 1:1 White Scar

Gold trim 

● Base - Liberator Gold 

● Soft shade - Wyldwood  

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Internal cloth colour and plumes 

● Base - Rakarth Flesh 2:1 Karak Stone 

● Soft shade - Karak Stone 

● Deep shade - Karak Stone 1:1 Dryad Bark 

● Chunky Highlight - Rakarth Flesh 

● Highlight - Rakarth Flesh 1:1 Pallid Wych Flesh 

● Highlight - Pallid Wych Flesh 

● Highlight/ Dot - White Scar 

External purple colour 

● Base - Phoenician Purple 

● Soft Shade - Phoenician Purple 2:1 Abaddon Black 

● Deep Shade - Abaddon Black 

● Glaze/ Chunky Highlight - Xereus Purple 

● Highlight - Xereus Purple 1:1 Genestealer Purple 

● Highlight - Genestealer Purple 

● Edge - Genestealer Purple + Dechala Lilac (if needed)

(Above) A Custodian wearing the black armour with purple detail of the Templi Prudentia, along with a white helmet plume. The cloak’s outer face is purple and its lining is ivory white. 


(Above) This Caladius grav-tank bears the same sombre polished black armour with purple in-fills as the Custodians it accompanies to battle. Its primary battle honour – ‘Maulland Sen’ – is worn proudly on its flanks, though it truth it will have served in countless battles throughout the long Wars of Unity and the Great Crusade. 

The Templi Veritas 

The final division of the Templii Magisterium Tertia is that whose role was shielded most ardently from those outside of the Imperial Household, for its implications and history were fell indeed. Its remit was that of the executioner: the eradication of any element held unworthy by the Emperor, be it due to betrayal or simple obsolescence, such that not even its memory endured. It is believed to have been the Custodians of this ‘Templi Veritas’ which enacted the cull of the Thunder Warriors at Mount Ararat, and who saw to the disposal of those deemed tainted in the final days of the second Rangdan campaign, alongside countless other grim duties all but erased from memory. 

During and following the Horus Heresy, they were the most bellicose of the Legio Custodes, and where their conquests were unable to scour all trace of their foe from existence, they were instead conducted with symbolic precision, inflicting pinpoint destruction upon worlds such as Chemos and Arachnus as harrowing displays of the Emperor’s judgement. Within this era, the number of Custodians active as part of the Templi Veritas defied all outside understanding of the Legio Custodes’ strength, especially in light of the bloody Webway conflict, leading some to suppose that, in secret, the Templi Veritas had been in the midst of shadowed preparations for some purge yet to come when the Horus Heresy erupted.

Custodians pursuing the goals of the Templi Veritas often adopt an armour of pale brass, sometimes with black in-fills, and with cloaks of black. 

Suggested paints 

Armour

● Base - Runelord Brass 

● Soft shade - Wyldwood  

● Deep Shade - Rhinox Hide 

● Highlight - Runelord Brass 1:1 Stormhost Silver 

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Black armour and cloth 

● Basecoat - Abaddon Black 

● Chunky Highlight - Eshin Grey 1:1 Corvus Black 

● Highlight - Eshin Grey 

● Highlight - Dawnstone 

● Highlight - Administratum Grey 

● Spots - Administratum Grey 1:1 White Scar

Red plume 

● Basecoat - Mephiston Red  

● Soft shade - Barak-Nar Burgundy 

● Deepshade - Barak-Nar Burgundy + Abaddon Black (selectively, mainly where separate bits of cloth meet) 

● Chunky Highlight - Evil Sunz Scarlet 

● Highlight - Wild Rider Red 

● Highlight - Wild Rider Red + Ungor Flesh 

● Highlight - Add more Ungor Flesh 

● Dots - Ungor Flesh 

● Smooth - Evil Sunz Scarlet

(Above) A Custodian wearing the pale brass armour and black loincloth and cloak of the Templi Veritas, indicating current or ongoing service under the purview of that order. 

(Above) The livery of this Caladius Annihilator grav-tank echoes the pale brass armour and black in-fills displayed on the auramite warplate of Custodians serving the mission of the Templi Veritas. 

Further Variation 

Suggested paints 

Gold Armour 

● Base - Retributor Armour 

● Soft shade - Darkoath Flesh 

● Deep shade - Cygor Brown 

● Edge Highlight - Liberator Gold 

● Extreme edges - Stormhost Silver 

Light gold Armour - 

● Base - Liberator Gold 

● Soft shade - Wyldwood  

● Highlight - Stormhost Silver 

Purple cloth and plume colour 

● Base: Phoenician Purple 

● Soft Shade: Phoenician Purple 2:1 Abaddon Black 

● Deep Shade: Abaddon Black 

● Glaze/ Chunky Highlight : Xereus Purple 

● Highlight : Xereus Purple 1:1 Genestealer Purple 

● Highlight: Genestealer Purple 

● Edge: Genestealer Purple + Dechala Lilac

(Above) This Custodian is wearing the standard gold of the Legio Custodes, but his cloak and helmet plume are the purple of the Templi Prudentia, indicating his long-term allegiance to that order’s goals, regardless of his current mission or duty. Similarly, guardians with a particular attachment to the other Templii might combine elements of that order’s distinctive variant livery with the more standard gold for which the Legio is most well known. 

The new Journal Tactica book that examines the Legio Custodes’ secret war in the Signus Cluster – against hordes of Slaaneshi daemons – is available to pre-order now, along with a range of plastic kits for Custodian squads and vehicles. Join the Ten Thousand and wield Humanity’s ultimate power on the battlefields of the Horus Heresy.

item.title: Fyreslayers in Battletome: Khazalite Holds – What you need to know
item.description: What’s happening to Grimnir’s faithful berzerkers?
item.content:encoded:
With the imminent arrival of Battletome: Khazalite Holds, the Fyreslayers find their new home and faction – see exactly which units will be in the new book.

Fyreslayers have existed since the earliest days of Warhammer Age of Sigmar, and there are loads of you with armies who might be wondering what this means for you and your collection.

First, this is a great opportunity to expand your Fyreslayers army into a wider duardin force. The Fyreslayers play an important role in the Khazalite Holds, as aggressive and hot-headed assault troops and monsters to complement the guns, artillery, and stalwart defence of the Kromdron.

However, if you just love Fyreslayers and want to continue playing with an army composed entirely of Grimnir’s fanatical followers, you absolutely can, either by just selecting Fyreslayers units in your army or by choosing the Fyrd of Fyrepeak Army of Renown.

The merge does mean that there are some units that will not feature in the new battletome. These units will soon come off sale, but they will remain usable in competitive events for a year after the new book releases, before moving into Warhammer Legends. This gives you 12 months to give them a last glorious tour of your local Warhammer events, while you ponder your future army compositions.

The Fyreslayers previously had a lot of infantry heroes, and four of these leave the army, along with the Magmic Invocations and Magmic Battleforge.

Vulkite Berzerkers are also moving to Legends. This one is likely the most impactful, as this unit was the mainstay of several armies, and their removal pivots the Fyreslayers into a more elite force, looking to the Hearthguard and Flameseekers to function as the armies infantry, backed up by Magmadroths and characters.

Fyreslayers units in Battletome: Khazalite Holds:

  • Auric Runefather on Magmadroth

  • Auric Runeson on Magmadroth

  • Auric Runesmiter on Magmadroth 

  • Auric Runefather 

  • Auric Runeson 

  • Auric Runesmiter 

  • Auric Flamekeeper 

  • Grimhold Exile 

  • Vulkyn Flameseekers 

  • Auric Hearthguard 

  • Hearthguard Berzerkers

  • Ormyr and Ashtongue (New!)

  • Honourable Mention: Gotrek Gurnisson*

Fyreslayers units moving to Warhammer Legends:

  • Vulkite Berzerkers

  • Auric Runemaster

  • Battlesmith

  • Doomseeker

  • Grimwrath Berzerker

  • Magmic Battleforge

  • Magmic Invocations

The new Khazalite Holds range will be up for pre-order very soon, so keep an eye out for up-to-date news here on Warhammer Community. 

* Not technically a Fyreslayer, but we’d hate for him to hold a grudge because we didn't include him in the list.

item.title: Using Slaanesh Daemons in the Age of Darkness: Designers’ notes
item.description: The team behind Warhammer: The Horus Heresy talk about the insidious new rules.
item.content:encoded:
The new Horus Heresy Journal Tactica introduces rules for using Slaaneshi Daemons in the Age of Darkness. The Battle for the Signus Cluster – Assault on Kol is available to pre-order now, so we sat down with the team behind the game to learn more.

Warhammer: The Horus Heresy Team: Following on from the first part of our Designers’ Notes on the latest Journal Tactica, we are going to take a closer look at the portion of the rules content that covers the Traitors, in particular, the Daemons of Slaanesh Army List. The Army List itself is a sub-faction of Daemons of the Ruinstorm, much like the previous Tzeentch Army List from the last Journal. As such, it functions in much the same way. Daemons of Slaanesh are able to be taken as part of an entirely Daemon-based army, or can be included as an Allied Faction in other Traitor armies.

Of course, the finer details of including Slaaneshi Daemons in your armies are detailed in the Army List itself, including the restrictions imposed by the Alignment of Ruinous Powers.* 

Before we delve into the specific Units within the list though, it is important to clarify why Slaaneshi Daemons, and indeed Daemons identified as belonging to any of the four cardinal powers, have a place in the Horus Heresy setting…

Imperial Understanding of Daemonkind

During the Horus Heresy, and even the later stages of the Great Crusade, daemonic incursion from the Warp and into realspace was unknown by all but the most guarded, secretive and clandestine organisations within the Imperium. Outside of these veiled chambers, the rest of the Imperium was blissfully unaware of the threat that resided in the Immaterium. What had so far been witnessed by Humanity had been hastily hushed and stifled by agents of the Imperium, acting to control the spread of information, ostensibly seeking to secure the wider safety of human colonies and limit their exposure to something that was already recognised as existentially dangerous. Much had been dismissed and explained away as aberrant xenos mutants or genetic malformations, because it was thought that even knowledge of the fundamental nature of such beings was a corrupting, malignant influence, and could lead to sedition against the Emperor.

Within extremely limited circles of the Imperial Household, records that detailed potential incursions were kept, documenting the truth of the matter and identifying the scale of the threat. Most of these records detailed what was categorised as “Ruinstorm” Daemons; these were manifestations of a general kind, that did not exhibit recognisable patterns in form or behaviour. Later analysis of these records showed that such incursions formed the majority of “daemonic activity” in the earlier stages, however as time progressed, more and more reports of Daemons following specific, divergent strains of form and character were logged.

From hierarchies of pustulent bringers of rot and decay, to feudal bands of blood-drenched beasts, fuelled by rage and violence, each of these strains were witnessed and recorded as distinctly different to each other, exhibiting different proclivities within the material realm. Interrogation of condemned individuals such debased cultist followers and demagogue preachers, captured on worlds across the Imperium, and the analysis of information gathered therein, allowed Imperial authorities to learn of Daemons and their true provenance. The very act of doing so was known to send sane men insane, reducing upright adepts of the Imperium to raving madmen who clawed at their own flesh throughout night and day, tormented by hellish visions conjured by their corrupted minds.

Their learnings were inscribed and bound within ward-sealed tomes, treated with even greater levels of care and sensitivity than the most volatile of alchemical substances, and stored in the deepest and most secure dungeons, under the Emperor’s authority. Only the most privileged agents of the Imperium were allowed access, usually as a matter of utmost necessity and under the most restrictive clearance levels. Those that could prove their commitment or resistance to corruption may be allowed to delve into the archives of daemonology, but to do so required submission to a range of conditions, including post-integration, psych-evaluation and an ensuing lifetime of scrutiny and suspicion. Only with the perspective of hindsight gained in the wake of the Horus Heresy, did Imperial scholars name the four major dominions of Daemon – Nurgle, Khorne, Slaanesh, and Tzeentch.

The Daemons of Excess

It is well known that hideous, yet graceful, manifestations that juxtapose lithe beauty with horrifying mutation are often the followers of the Chaos God Slaanesh. It is just these Daemons that are introduced in the new Journal Tactica. 

All relevant Models from this new Army List gain access to the Blissful Pain Gambit in Challenges, where your champion responds to the stimulating effect of wounds suffered. In game, this increases the amount of attacks a Model can make in a Challenge based on how many Wounds their opponent has doled out (even if those Wounds are saved!)

Blissful Pain

To the followers of Slaanesh, there is no difference between pleasure or pain, elation or terror – only the amplitude of the emotion experienced matters. So it is that wounds that would otherwise lay another combatant low, instead serve to excite and invigorate the debased thralls of the Prince of Excess.

The Controlling Player gains attacks during the Strike Step for each Wound inflicted upon them, whether the Wounds are saved or not.

This Gambit may be selected once per Challenge. When selected, the Opposing Player gains Challenge Advantage without any Focus Roll being made. However, for each successful Wound Test made by the Opposing Player in the Strike Step, the Model this Gambit was selected for has their Attacks Characteristic modified by +2 for the duration of that Strike Step.

Slaanesh Daemons can also make the Battlelust Advanced Reaction, driving them into a frenzy when subjected to the heady sights and sounds of battle. This allows them to move forward when targeted by a Ranged Attack, also gaining a +1 Initiative Modifier during the following turn. This will force opponents to choose their targets carefully, as Slaaneshi Daemons close in on their ranks, lest they provoke a murderous frenzy within their ranks.

There’s also a new Psychic Discipline known as Enraptura, which allows its practitioners to use the Psychic Power Beguile to transfix and allure opposing Units and prevent them from making Reactions triggered by Units with the Slaanesh Trait. There’s also Malignity, which comes in the form of a Psychic Weapon, representing a whispered suggestion from the god Slaanesh, that the target should turn on their squadmates and attack them by any means necessary!**

The Units

On to the Units in the Army List itself. At the top is the Herald of Slaanesh in the Command Role. These harbingers of excess are fast Infantry models with a reasonably high Initiative Characteristic of 5, improved by the Impact (I) Special Rule. Whilst they are competent fighters, their primary role is to summon in their kin using the Herald of Unreality Special rule.

Next are the hideously swift Slaaneshi Seekers. A Fast Attack option for the army, these are a manoeuvrable and hard hitting close combat Unit that relies heavily on getting the charge off. Even Space Marines need to be wary of their Razorclaws.

Razorclaws

Rending (6+), Breaching (6+), Phage (WP)

Immaterial

Slaaneshi Fiends fill a Heavy Assault slot and provide a reasonably swift, hard hitting assault Unit, that with 5 Wounds apiece will be able to weather some damage before they fall. Fortunately for the armies of the Imperium, these monsters only come in Units of three!

Daemonettes form the Troops role in the army and as expected, they are light on their feet and hit hard on the charge with the Impact (I) Special Rule. In big units of up to 20 Models, Dameonettes will shred through enemy infantry with their Razorclaws, and thanks to the Exquisite Suffering Special Rule, will gain Combat Resolution points when their opponents fail Feel No Pain rolls. Situational? Sure, but it’s certainly very thematic. 

Of course, the biggest and baddest Daemon in the list is the Keeper of Secrets, a Greater Daemon of Slaanesh. As a Paragon Unit, these beasts can go toe-to-toe with the heroes of the Imperium and can be equipped with either a fearsome Shimmerblade or a Shimmerspear and shield, which avails them with the Deflect Special Rule, allowing them to bat aside an enemy Hit Test result of a 6, turning it into a result of a 1.

Favoured of Slaanesh

Slaanesh doesn’t just provide for its daemonic offspring, and the benevolence of the Lord of Excess also extends to the Traitor Legions. A Legiones Astartes Army with an Esoterist may include the Rapturous Host Auxiliary Detachment, allowing a well-rounded gaggle of Daemon Units to be included in the force. 

Additionally, the Insidious Corruption upgrade may be applied to the following models for +20 points, adding to them the Malefic Sub-Type.

• Praetor

• Praetor with Jump Pack

• Cataphractii Praetor

• Tartaros Praetor

• Saturnine Praetor

With a whole new army list at their disposal and boons to the existing Legiones Astartes list, the Traitor host matching on Terra will doubtlessly be swelled, leaving us to wonder, how will the Loyalists begin to counter these threats? You’ll have to wait and see what joins the muster in the next Journal Tactica!

Thanks, folks! Pre-order Journal Tactica: The Battle for The Signus Cluster – Assault on Kol and get ready to unleash the forces of Slaanesh in the Age of Darkness.

* That’s which Daemons get on with which other Daemons, to you and me.
** Just in case there’s not enough treachery in the Age of Darkness already.

item.title: Imperial Knights star in a new Black Library novel
item.description: The Winter Knight rides out into a dying world, plus new versions of fan-favourite books.
item.content:encoded:
The new Black Library novel Throne Questoris puts you in the Throne Mechanicum of an ancient war machine on a quest to defend a dying world.

Though knightly scion Asrien Balateur is only moments away from claiming the throne that is their birthright, the land itself is being swallowed by mysterious snowstorms, and Imperial Knights are disappearing among shattered castles and ravaged realms. 

The petty squabbles of quarrelsome barons and pressures of a king’s court are no longer the biggest of Asrien’s worries. Madness rises from the planet’s murky past, and only the future king can hope to rally the land against debts long since forgotten.

The land moves, and the Winter Knight rides.

With a combination of posturing, intrigue, and action, Throne Questoris by Victoria Hayward offers fresh ways to explore the 41st Millennium.

And it’s not the only Warhammer 40,000 novel that we’re showing off today.

The classic novel Cypher: Lord of the Fallen by John French is the next release in Black Library’s line of Illustrated and Annotated Editions. Relive the enigmatic rogue’s escape from Holy Terra with a new introduction from the author and commentary throughout, brightened up by all-new illustrations that really set the scene for Cypher’s flight.

Ben Counter’s Grey Knights is also returning to the Black Library in a new, suitably ornate Special Edition.

This novel is one of the finest windows into the day-to-day of the Grey Knights Chapter and their eternal war against the empyrean. A mortally wounded daemonhunter banishes a powerful daemon back to the Warp for a thousand years, but as we know, that’s not necessarily a long time on the scale of Warhammer 40,000.

A thousand years is up, and Ghargatuloth is back for more havoc, but he didn’t contend on one thing – a waiting party of Grey Knights who knew exactly when and where their quarry would arrive. Unfortunately for the knights of Titan, the daemon’s return is part of a perilous prophecy, and their task will be a little more complicated than simply gunning the offending heretic down.

All three of these books will be available to pre-order soon. In the meantime, get started on reading about Imperial Knights with Kingsblade, Knightsblade, and Knights of the Imperium – all available now on the Black Library app.

item.title: Space Marine 2 gets a massive anniversary update
item.description: Celebrate the start of Year 3 with a new weapon and play as Chaos Space Marines in Siege Mode.
item.content:encoded:
A new update is out today for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2, with a new weapon, new chances to play as dastardly heretics, and new challenges for the most daring players.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Let’s start with the new Champion pack. The Space Wolves send one of their best with an incredible new armour set based on the Wolf Guard Battle Leader, complete with a round Fenrisian storm shield so you can use it with the Bulwark class. 

This modified MkX Tacticus suit is covered in furs and fangs befitting one of the Chapter’s most storied veterans.

But wait, what’s that he’s holding up there? From today, players can bash xenos skulls in and sunder Rubric power armour with a mighty one-handed thunder hammer! This brutal weapon is faster than the two-handed variant and can charge up to deal rippling area-of-effect blows, making it a great option for all kinds of foes.

Players using the Tactical, Assault, Bulwark, and Techmarines classes can all take the one-handed thunder hammer into battle, and there’s even a powerful Heroic version – the Power Maul.

These come alongside top-end additions for the power axe, auto bolt rifle, and five new cosmetic items bought with Accolades, including a fancy shoulderpad for the Black Templars and an Iron Halo.

The Tactical class is getting a top-to-bottom rework in this patch, renovating large swathes of its skill tree to offer more varied and interesting build options. It will also be getting access to the one-handed thunder hammer, the power axe, and the power sword, though with any of these powerful melee options equipped, you’ll lose access to your primary weapon.

So what if you want to take a bolt rifle and a power axe? There’s actually a Signature Perk for that – replacing the old Signal Jammer, you’ll now be able to choose an option that lets you take the regular, humble bolt rifle in your secondary weapon slot, with progression shared with its normal primary slot version. Tactical specialists really are the most versatile Space Marines in the squad.

If you’re looking for more of a challenge to test out the new skills, or simply enjoy running through Operations as close to the wire as possible, try out the new Crucible mode to earn Crucible XP. By talking to the Company Chaplain on board the battle barge you can activate Penances – personal debuffs that make your run harder – and completing missions with them active will put you on track to earning a set of Lamenters armour pieces.

Alongside the Space Wolves Champion Pack, the mysterious Exorcists Chapter also gets a Cosmetic Pack added to the Season Pass. This set of stylised armour pieces includes one Helmet, two Left and Right Pauldrons, two Left and Right Gauntlets, and one Breastplate from everyone’s favourite daemon-hunting Successor Chapter, covered in purity seals and arcane script.  The Space Wolves Champion pack and Exorcists Chapter Pack are available to buy individually and also as part of Season Pass 3, whilst everything else included in the update is free. 

Fancy getting a bit traitorous? A new spin on the wave-based Siege mode lets you step into the boots of a Chaos Space Marine to slaughter Tyranids, Imperial Guardsmen, and even loyalist Space Marines as you fight for dominion over Avarax. The new mode will initially include two sectors, with a third planned for a later release.

On top of all of this, we’ve still got room for a few more free additions. Heroic weapon variants of the power axe, one-handed thunder hammer, and auto bolt rifle will be added to the armoury, along with five new armour pieces and an expansion of the wargear sharing system. A third slot will open up to be used with capes, tabards, and iron halos, while some new items for Vanguard, Heavy, and Assault classes can be unlocked with new Ordeals.

This is only the first big update coming over the next 12 months, and the Year 3 battle plan is stacked with enough new content to fill a battle barge, from new weapons and new operations to an entirely new class – the Apothecary! Check out our first look at the schedule.

And that just about covers it! Head into Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 now to try out the new update, and get yourself prepared for Year 3.

item.title: Adeptus Custodes: Top Detachment Tips
item.description: Here are some collectively collated combos to get the most out of the Ten Thousand.
item.content:encoded:
We’ve shown the Adeptus Custodes’ new army rules and detachments, so today we’re looking at some detachment combinations to help you hit the ground running when the codex drops.

We’ve put together a couple of options for detachment combos, and give some advice on units you could use to make the biggest impact on the battlefield.

Even Harder to Kill

  • Shadowkeepers (1 Detachment Point)

  • Honoured Companions (1 Detachment Point)

  • Null Maiden Vigil (1 Detachment Point)

This detachment combination would be useful with Custodian Guard Sodality and Custodian Wardens forming the backbone of your army, led by Shield-Captains and supported by units of Witchseeker Squads.

The Custodian Wardens are some of the hardest nuts to crack in the new Codex, their Living Fortress ability giving attacks against them -1 AP. When on an objective, they (and other Adeptus Custodes units) will benefit from attacks against them having -1 to wound rolls if the attack’s Strength is higher than their Toughness, thanks to the Wardens of the Dark Cells detachment rule. Equip them with castellan axes to counter some of the most elite enemies in the galaxy and, with support from the Companion’s Watch detachment rule and the Avenge the Fallen stratagem,* you’ll be throwing out upwards of 15 attacks at 10 S, -2 AP, 4 D, re-rolling wound rolls of 1. 

DETACHMENT RULES

HONOURED COMPANIONS

COMPANION’S WATCH

Among the Companions and the Sentinel Guard, vigilance is the most crucial of attributes.

While a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit is within range of an objective, that unit’s attacks can re-roll wound rolls of 1.

More excitingly, if you don’t end up needing to use the Avenge the Fallen stratagem, the Emperor’s Domain stratagem in your opponent’s Fight phase allows you to make a consolidation move out of combat provided you end that move on an objective. As this happens after your opponent has already consolidated, you’ll be primed and ready to shoot and charge your foes once again in your own turn. An excellent use of 1CP.

AVENGE THE FALLEN (1CP)

HONOURED COMPANIONS STRATAGEM

The loss of a single Custodian is commemorated by the tolling of the Bell of Lost Souls on Terra, and by their comrades’ bloody vengeance on the battlefield

WHEN: Fight phase, when a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit that is below starting strength is selected to fight.

TARGET: That TRUSTED SENTINEL unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit’s melee attacks (excluding those made by CHARACTER models) have +2 A.

EMPEROR’S DOMAIN (1CP)

HONOURED COMPANIONS STRATAGEM

There are those territories that must remain in the hands of the Imperium and be free of foes, regardless of the cost. 

WHEN: Fight phase, when a friendly TRUSTED SENTINEL unit is selected to make a consolidation move.

TARGET: That TRUSTED SENTINEL unit. 

EFFECT: You can select the objective consolidation mode for that consolidation move, regardless of that consolidation move’s Before Moving restrictions.

This means your unit can move out of engagement range with enemy units, provided it meets the conditions of the objective consolidation mode.

Meanwhile your Custodian Guard Sodality will be better used as a crowbar to pry enemies from objectives, using their Impenetrable Defence ability to gain Sustained Hits 1 against anything that isn’t a Monster or Vehicle.

The Shield-Captains could be attached to either of these units, as they will allow you to either use two different ka’tah abilities in the same battle round, or one in your and your opponent’s turns, allowing your units to exercise total flexibility in all situations.

DETACHMENT RULES

NULL MAIDEN VIGIL

SILENT SISTERHOOD

The Null Maidens of the Silent Sisterhood bring with them the nightmare pall of their collective null aura, afflicting their opponents with a creeping sense of dread.

  • When mustering your army, you can select a friendly ANATHEMA PSYKANA CHARACTER model to be your WARLORD.

  • Friendly PROSECUTOR SQUAD units have BATTLELINE.

  • Friendly ANATHEMA PSYKANA units have the following ability:

Creeping Dread (Aura): In the Battle-shock step of your opponent’s Command phase, each enemy unit within 12" of this unit that is a PSYKER unit/below starting strength makes a battle-shock roll, with -1 to that battle-shock roll.

In the case of some stubborn enemy units on objectives or problematic stratagem potentials, the Witchseekers can battle-shock your opponent’s units either by shooting them in your turn or using the Creeping Dread ability from the Null Maiden Vigil detachment to deny those more resilient units a chance to hold objectives or use stratagems.

Hyper-elite Fighting Machines

  • Dread Host (1 Detachment Point)

  • Lions of the Emperor (1 Detachment Point)

  • Might of the Moritoi (1 Detachment Point)

This combination is all about maximising your melee superiority, through the mobility of Terminators backed up by Dreadnoughts.

Through the Lions of the Emperor detachment rule, your Terminator units have total board control, by being able to return to strategic reserves, allowing them to reappear later wherever the need is most dire.** This is especially potent if you include a variety of Terminator units in your army, as each excels against specific targets. 

DETACHMENT RULES
LIONS OF THE EMPEROR

ON GILDED WINGS

Terminator sodalities are swept up by golden drop craft, ready to be deployed once more as battle demands.

At the end of your opponent’s Fight phase, if a friendly ADEPTUS CUSTODES TERMINATOR unit is unengaged, you can place that unit in strategic reserves.

Allarus Custodians are excellent at bringing down even the most towering of foes, Aquilon Terminators with solarite power gauntlets want to break apart elite infantry and light vehicles, and those with solarite power talons want to find the nearest horde and wipe it out. Their manoeuvrability means you can always apply the correct tool in the right location, and makes it difficult for your opponent to react to your next move.

Dread Host allows your Terminator units to have dramatically improved chances of making a charge after arriving from strategic reserves, by giving you a crucial charge re-roll. You can put the odds further in your favour by using the Fury of the Emperor stratagem to get +2 to that charge roll, while still re-rolling if required.

A Telemon Heavy Dreadnought or two make an already terrifying army even scarier for your opponent. They now sport a near Primarch-level statline, and one of these might just be your best answer to fighting against another Custodes army.***

One of these units can be given the Memento Moritoi upgrade, which gives your unit +1 A, S, and D to its melee attacks. Dual caestus fists are now A8 , S15, and D5. That’s a flattened Custodian Guard Sodality every time you attack, and you’ll be re-rolling the wound roll to ensure you push the pain through.

These are just some suggestions to get you battling the enemies of the Golden Throne as quickly as possible, but we look forward to seeing what you come up with too when the new Codex goes up for pre-order on Saturday.

* Should any of your Wardens have fallen.
** Sometimes referred to as being “uppy downy”.
*** Here are some other things your vaunted Custodes need to look out for.

item.title: Warhammer 40,000 – Balance Update: Chaos, the Imperium and Xenos Fight Back
item.description: Learn what yesterday’s big changes mean for the non-Space Marines factions.
item.content:encoded:
The latest Warhammer 40,000 balance update dropped yesterday, making Space Marines of different kinds faster, tougher, and more deadly. But what do those changes mean for the other armies of the 41st Millennium?

An increase in AP on boltguns and chainswords is a new challenge to overcome for units universally. It will encourage some factions to pivot to defensively focused detachments, or units with an invulnerable save that is the same or better than their default save characteristic, to minimise this change on your army. This is also dependent on what role you want a unit to play in your army. 

For example, you are playing Tyranids and you have deployed Termagants to act as a screening* unit to protect your Excocrine from being charged by some Deep Striking Chaos Space Marine Terminators. Regardless of your opponent’s shooting, the Terminators are unable to charge your more important Exocrine due to the increased distance you created using your Termagants. Boltguns being more powerful doesn’t change the fact that your Termagants have fulfilled their purpose, and if your opponent has included more boltguns instead of a lascannon, a plasma gun, or a meltagun, then their efficacy against your more valuable Exocrine will be reduced.

There will also typically be fewer Space Marines on the battlefield to shoot or charge, likely meaning your opponent will be looking to maximise their points with the most effective units available to them, so boltguns and chainswords may be the least of your worries.

This also means that although Space Marines are tougher to kill now, fewer Space Marines on the battlefield means your own units also have fewer things to kill. In the above example, the Exocrine, although wounding them on a 3+ now, has fewer to kill, and offers more value through each one it does destroy. 

As Space Marine variants make up the majority of armies within Warhammer 40,000, it’s generally wise to construct your army assuming you will be battling them at some point. Many of the units that were good at killing Space Marines are still good at it. Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Doomsday Arks, Howling Banshees, Riptides, and Knight Despoilers will continue to cause problems for the Adeptus Astartes.

So having broken down what the impacts are, what are the upsides to this change for you?

As we’ve said, there are going to be fewer Space Marine bodies actually on the battlefield, which will change how they approach the game. They won’t be able to trade** for objectives as well as many non-Space Marine armies, and they will find it more challenging to hold down objectives and safely achieve secondary objectives. More horde-focussed armies such as Astra Militarum, Drukhari, and Genestealer Cults will be better equipped to trade bodies into the brutal meat grinder for that sweet victory.

The increase in strength to boltguns and chainswords has mixed degrees of value against your armies. For the average Human, Aeldari, Leman Russ, or Goliath Rock Grinder, this change means nothing, as it’s not enough to improve their odds to wound against these types of targets. 

This all comes with new strategies, new army compositions, new challenges, and new triumphs to achieve, all of which requires some trial and error to find the right way to approach and overcome. So don’t be disheartened if you don’t find your army running rampant across the fields of Chogoris or wastes of Baal immediately – even Abaddon took 13 tries to crack Cadia, remember?

Download the latest balance update now so you can be ready for whatever the Space Marines try and throw at you.

Download now

* A screening unit is one that is cheap in points and often used to deny your opponent movement. This might be through standing in the way and physically blocking opposing models, by denying areas of the board for units to arrive from strategic reserves, or to make it harder for your opponent to charge into another target.
** Trading means units that are typically more effective for their points cost at holding and challenging for objectives than their opponents, generally by destroying units more expensive in points than themselves.

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Quarterly Battlescroll Updates
item.description: See the latest rules updates from the Mortal Realms.
item.content:encoded:
We’re a few months into the season of Warhammer Age of Sigmar, so it’s time for the first of the quarterly Battlescroll updates. 

Points adjustments are complemented by some important rules changes to improve balance in the Mortal Realms and below you can find a summary of the most significant updates.

Universal

There are a couple of changes that open up list building options. Firstly, a number of infantry heroes can now be included in regiments, and a lot of units have had their reinforcement restrictions lifted. 

Grand Alliance Order

A couple of rules from the Scourge of Aqshy season rules have proven to be more powerful than anticipated and so are being toned down a little. Fyreslayers can no longer use Blazing Impetus to move after being set up, and for the Idoneth Deepkin, Abyssal Dweller no longer reduces enemy movement. The War Hydra from the Cities of Sigmar battletome supplement has also had its Impossible to Destroy ability tweaked as it was proving, well, impossible to destroy.

Grand Alliance Chaos

On the Skaven side, Krittok Foulblade can now use his A Reputation for Cunning ability without needing to spend a Command Point, and the Lightning Master ability of the Warlock Galvaneer is now guaranteed to activate, yes-yes! For the Slaves to Darkness the Oracular Visions of the Sorcerer Lord are now more reliable, but units with an Ensorcelled Banner can no longer switch Pledge to Chaos keywords. You chose your Dark God and now you’re stuck with them!

The newest addition to Grand Alliance Chaos – the Helsmiths of Hashut – have had their battle formations updated. The studio felt they were not having the impact hoped for and so the Zharrdron now have some new tools as they seek to claim dominion over the Mortal Realms.

Grand Alliance Death

The Nighthaunt have had the most changes in this quarter’s update with improvements to the Lord Vitriolic and Scriptor Mortis, while the Shadowy Aura heroic trait now blocks visibility to Nighthaunt infantry and cavalry, and there’s been a boost to the Death Stalkers battle formation. The Ossiarch Bonereapers no longer have to pay the Relentless Discipline ‘tax’ for reinforced units, so abilities such as Pitiless Assault just got cheaper for your larger units.

The Scourge of Aqshy Vengorian Lord has been proving slightly too powerful so the Soulblight Gravelords Monster Frenzied Surge ability has been adjusted.

Grand Alliance Destruction

Finally, the Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant from the Scourge of Aqshy has undergone a little change so that he doesn’t form an over-the-top combo with the new Rock-hurlers.
